description: A drum voice built from a tuned tone oscillator and a noise generator, crossfaded together and shaped by one envelope, after Bastl's Crust module

params.text: Sets the octave of the tone oscillator over a ten-octave range, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Octave
Sets the pitch envelope: clockwise gives a falling kick-style sweep, counter-clockwise a slower membrane sweep, and this is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Sweep
Detunes the second oscillator from the first: counter-clockwise by a fixed number of Hz, down into LFO speeds and independent of the pitch, clockwise by an exponential ratio reaching 16 to 1
Tunes the ratio between the two oscillators in fractions of an interval, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Stepped Detune
Shifts the tone oscillator by up to 12 semitones either way, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Semitone
Shifts the tone oscillator by up to 1 semitone either way, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Fine
Sweeps the tone oscillator smoothly across its whole frequency range, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Broad
Sets the pitch of the noise layer, which each noise algorithm reads its own way, and is what the PITCH knob does while the tune mode is Noise Param
Steps the PITCH knob to the next tune mode on each press; a long press swaps between the octave, sweep and detune set and the tune, semitone and fine-tune set, and a second long press leaves that
Crossfades the output between the tone layer and the noise layer
Steps the tone oscillator to the next mode on each press, through Dual, Ring Mod, FM and FM 2; a long press moves the PITCH knob onto the stepped detune and the ENV knob onto the pitch envelope decay
Sets the amplitude envelope applied to both the tone and the noise layer: clockwise lengthens the decay, counter-clockwise lengthens attack and decay together
Sets the decay time of the pitch envelope, shortest at the centre and following a different exponential curve to each side; this is what the ENV knob does after a long press of the tone mode button
Steps the noise generator to the next algorithm on each press, through Noise, Crunch, Metal and Clap; a long press moves the PITCH knob onto the noise tuning
Drives the voice into distortion, and is what the TIMBRE fader does while the timbre mode is Distortion
Sets the filter cutoff applied to the noise layer alone, and is what the TIMBRE fader does while the timbre mode is Filter
Reshapes the tone oscillator's waveform, and is what the TIMBRE fader does while the timbre mode is Shape
Steps the TIMBRE fader to the next timbre mode on each press, through Distortion, Filter and Shape; a long press starts choosing what the CTRL knob is assigned to
Sets whichever one parameter the control destination names, and adds to the voltage at the CTRL input when a cable is patched there

inputs.text: Adds to whatever the TIMBRE fader is set to at the moment, -5V to 5V covering the full travel of that fader
Adds to the LAYER fader, -5V to 5V covering the full crossfade between tone and noise
Adds to the CTRL knob, -5V to 5V covering the full range of whatever the control destination names
Scales the loudness of the hit, 0V silent and 10V full, and negative voltages read as 0V; with TRIG unpatched a voltage here fires the voice as well, above 1.5V to sound and back below 0.5V to rearm
Fires the drum on each rising edge past 1V
Sets the pitch of the tone oscillator, doubling its frequency for each volt
Adds to the ENV knob, -5V to 5V covering the full range of that knob

outputs.text: The amplitude envelope of the voice as a voltage, 0V at rest and 5V at the peak of a hit
The drum itself, the tone and noise layers crossfaded and enveloped, reaching 5V either way

notes: nothing sounds until a trigger arrives at TRIG; with TRIG unpatched a gate at VELOCITY fires the voice instead, and with neither patched the module is silent
fourteen factory presets are installed with the plugin, reached from the module's right-click menu under Preset
menu: Module Modes — a submenu gathering the four mode settings the panel buttons step through
Tune Mode: Octave, Sweep, Detune, Stepped Detune, Semitone, Fine, Broad, Noise Param — sets what the PITCH knob adjusts; inside Module Modes
Tone Mode: Dual, Ring Mod, FM, FM 2 — sets how the two oscillators of the tone layer combine; inside Module Modes
Noise Mode: Noise, Crunch, Metal, Clap — sets the noise algorithm; inside Module Modes
Timbre Mode: Distortion, Filter (noise only), Shape — sets what the TIMBRE fader adjusts; inside Module Modes
Control Destination — sets which one parameter the CTRL knob and the CTRL input act on, chosen from a list of sixteen covering tune, tone, noise, layer and timbre
Input Jack S&H — one switch per input jack, plus Set all inputs to use S&H and Set no inputs use S&H; a switched-on input is read only at the instant of a trigger and held until the next
Quantisation: None, Semitone — rounds the V/OCT input to whole semitones before it is used
Disable flashing light on trigger — stops the panel lights blinking each time the voice is triggered
